input.question: When companies have to cut the 5% of the budget why do a lot of employees get fired? Why can't they just cut 5% of salary from everyone?
input.ground_truth: A company's budget is usually much larger than what they pay everyone. Cutting 5% can amount to far, far more money than 5% of everyone's pay. Not to mention the amount of money most large companies spend on worker's benefits. Usually an employee "costs" more to have than what they're paid. So cutting 5% of their salary will never amount to cutting them out entirely.

Okay, let’s imagine the company is like a big family that has a piggy bank with money inside. This money is what they use to pay for everything, like rent, food, and also to pay everyone who helps in the family (these are the employees).

Now, let’s say the family finds out they don’t have as much money as before, so they have to use 5% less from their piggy bank. That means they have a little bit less money to spend.

If the family tries to take a tiny bit (5%) from everyone’s pocket money, it might not be enough to fix the problem, because maybe they need to save a bigger amount.

Instead, sometimes the family has to make bigger changes. Maybe they decide that they can’t pay for as many helpers anymore, so they have to let some people go. That way, they save the money they were using to pay those helpers’ salaries.

So, it’s not always easy to just take a little bit from everyone, because sometimes the problem is too big for that, and they have to make bigger changes like letting some people go to save more money.
